summary.oneLiner: Strong Q4 FY26 performance driven by pellet and rolled product ramp-up, with EBITDA margin holding at 23% despite softer realizations; key catalysts are the 20GW BESS, 1Mn ton integrated steel plant, and 540MW solar expansion, positioning GPIL as a vertically integrated low-carbon steel and energy transition player.
summary.business: GPIL operates an integrated steel value chain that begins with captive iron ore mining and beneficiation, moves through high-grade magnetite pelletisation at Siltara, Raipur, sponge iron (DRI) and billet-making at its Steel Melting Shop, and ends in rolled long products, structural sections and hot-dip galvanised fabricated structures. Ferro alloys (silico-manganese) are manufactured through group entities at Urla Industrial Area, Raipur, while a captive renewable portfolio of solar, waste heat recovery, biomass and wind power supplies the manufacturing operations. Products are almost entirely intermediate industrial goods sold to construction and infrastructure, to the power transmission and renewable energy sector (where GPIL holds PGCIL certification), and to other steelmakers and re-rollers; exports are a negligible share of turnover.

Mining and pellets: High-grade magnetite iron ore pellets (approximately 65% iron content, low alumina and low phosphorus)
Finished long steel: Structural Rolled Products - angles, channels, beams and joists, produced at RR Ispat
Value-added fabrication: Galvanised Fabricated Products - hot-dip galvanised precision-engineered structures
Power: Captive renewable power - solar, waste heat recovery (WHRB), biomass and wind
Under development: Cold Rolling Mill complex output - ZAM, galvalume, colour-coat and cold rolled coils
Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) through Godawari New Energy Private Limited

currentContext.expansion: FY 2025-26 was framed as the year GPIL secured the approvals and commissioned the assets that unlock its next growth phase, with the Board approving four major strategic initiatives that together form a growth roadmap towards a revenue target of approximately Rs.30,000 crores by 2031. The 2 MnT iron ore pellet plant was commissioned in December 2025, lifting total pellet capacity 74% from 2.7 MnT to 4.7 MnT; it is described as the first plant in India to deploy natural gas-based Grate-Kiln pelletisation, replacing coal gas and cutting CO2 by roughly 2 lakh tonnes a year. Q4 FY 2025-26 was its first full quarter, at 78% utilisation, guided to 85% in FY27. On the mining side, Consent to Operate for the Ari Dongri iron ore mines at an enhanced 6 MnT was received from CECB in February 2026 (up from 2.35 MnT), described as the single most important de-risking event of the year and taking total captive ore capacity to 6.7 MnT including Boria Tibu 0.7 MnT; phased ramp-up begins in FY27 with full-scale operations targeted from FY28. A beneficiation plant at the mine site received Environment Clearance and Consent to Set Up on 31 January 2026 for expansion from 2.35 MnT to 6 MnT, with commissioning targeted for Q3 FY 2026-27. Other Consents to Operate received in the year enhanced sponge iron capacity from 0.594 MnT to 0.65 MnT, HB Wire from 0.1 MnT to 0.115 MnT, and added 7 MW of waste heat recovery power to take total WHRP capacity to 49 MW. Three build-out projects follow. The 0.7 MnT CRM Complex at Sarora (Tilda, Raipur) for cold rolled, GL/ZAM, Alu Silicon/GI and colour-coated steel carries a capex of Rs.900 crore funded by Rs.550 crore of sanctioned bank debt plus internal accruals, on 452 acres already acquired and shared with the Integrated Steel Plant, and is registered under PLI 1.1 and PLI 1.2; equipment orders have been placed for the Pickling Line, two CGL lines, the Colour Coating Line and the Acid Regeneration Plant. The 1 MnT Integrated Steel Plant for structural steel and wire rods via the blast furnace route is envisaged at Rs.7,000 crores on a 1:1 debt-equity basis, with environment approval granted and Consent to Establish awaited. A 20 GWh BESS manufacturing plant is being executed through 100% subsidiary Godawari New Energy Private Limited on 112 acres in the AURIC Industrial Area, Maharashtra, with Maharashtra government incentives approved and a Tier-1 supply chain secured (EVE Power LFP cells, ROCHE Energy BOS, FIMER India PCS); the Directors' Report separately describes a 40 GWh BESS project in two phases at a total cost of Rs.1625 crores including working capital margin money, plus a 45 MWh BESS at the Mahurmkala solar plant for about Rs.40 crores. Captive solar is being tripled from 165 MW to 540 MW to power the mines, the additional pellet capacity, the CRM and the ISP: 25 MW commissioned, 100 MW under construction, and 250 MW with land in possession aligned to ISP and CRM commissioning. CAUTION - the bundle carries internally inconsistent dates and quanta for the same projects: the CRM is variously given commissioning of August 2027 (Corporate Overview initiative panel), March 2027 (Chairman deep-dive and project table) and construction start of August 2026 versus July 2026; the ISP construction start is given as November 2026 in one place and October 2026 in another with commissioning targeted FY 2029-30; the 100 MW solar is given commissioning of July 2026 in the Corporate Overview and Q2FY27 in the Directors' Report; the 25 MW solar is dated May 2026 in the Directors' Report and 19 May 2026 in the Corporate Overview; and BESS capex appears as Rs.1,400 crores (Corporate Overview / Chairman) and Rs.1625 crores for the full 40 GWh in the Directors' Report. Existing captive solar is stated as 165 MW in the Corporate Overview but the MD&A describes a renewable portfolio of 190 MW of solar.

risks.risk: Operational risk - equipment failure and unplanned shutdowns across six integrated manufacturing units
risks.note: Equipment failure, unplanned shutdowns or maintenance issues at the mining, pelletisation, sponge iron, steelmaking or power generation facilities can hit production continuity, efficiency and profitability. Because the units are vertically integrated, the AR notes a disruption in any one unit can have cascading effects on downstream production. Mitigants cited: structured preventive maintenance, an AI-enabled Integrated Control Room monitoring operations 24x7, and strategic inventory buffers for critical raw materials and spares.

risks.risk: Input and raw material price and availability risk
risks.note: Prices and availability of iron ore, coking coal, coke, ferro alloys, natural gas and energy inputs directly drive production costs, margins and competitiveness, and are exposed to global supply chain disruption, geopolitics, import competition and trade policy. Partially offset by captive iron ore with 35+ years of supply security, a long-term supply MoU with GAIL India Limited, and a beneficiation plant that reduces external ore procurement - but the MD&A also notes overall raw material cost rose because of higher consumption of iron ore purchased from the market.

Steel, iron ore and pellet realisations follow global commodity cycles driven by China demand, global overcapacity and demand cyclicality across construction, infrastructure, automotive and manufacturing; global excess steelmaking capacity may exert sustained downward pressure on realisations. This is the risk that actually bit in FY 2025-26 - the company describes lower realisations across all products except ferro alloys and galvanised fabricated products. Mitigants: vertical integration, the merchant pellet premium from high-grade 65% Fe quality, product mix diversification and export flexibility.

risks.risk: Project execution and commissioning risk across a large concurrent capex programme
risks.note: The Company is simultaneously executing the CRM Complex, Integrated Steel Plant, BESS manufacturing, solar expansion and the beneficiation plant. Delays in implementation, regulatory approvals, equipment delivery or commissioning, or cost overruns, may impact expected returns and strategic timelines; equipment lead times from global suppliers, contractor capacity constraints and multi-regulatory approval sequences all create execution risk across several concurrent projects. Mitigants: a structured project execution framework, a dedicated management team and Board-level oversight per project, and phased capex sequencing.

risks.risk: Financial and leverage risk from the scale of the capex programme
risks.note: Large-scale capital expenditure, if not managed within prudent guardrails, may raise leverage and finance costs and constrain financial flexibility. The AR flags a marginal deterioration in the debt-equity ratio (0.07x in FY26 versus 0.06x in FY25) reflecting early project borrowings, and states the ratio is expected to rise modestly as the ISP and BESS ramp up. Guardrails cited: a 1:1 debt-equity limit on all major projects with the equity component funded entirely from internal accruals and no equity dilution planned, operating cash flow fully funding FY 2026-27 capex without additional borrowing, a net cash position, and debt lined up before construction begins.

risks.risk: Regulatory and environmental risk, including mining approvals and carbon regulation
risks.note: Mining operations need continuous compliance with environmental clearances, Consent to Operate, Consent to Set Up and forest clearances; any delay in obtaining or renewing approvals may disrupt mining and production continuity. This is not theoretical for GPIL - the FY26 mining ramp was constrained by CTO timing at Ari Dongri, with the approval only received in February 2026. Increasingly stringent environmental regulation and decarbonisation commitments may require substantial additional capital expenditure, and the EU CBAM, fully operational from January 2026, imposes a carbon cost on steel imports based on embedded CO2 intensity. Energy management is separately flagged as the top material issue in BRSR - a highly energy-intensive industry facing penalties for exceeding emission limits and rising compliance costs.

Manufacturing facilities, captive mines and power generation assets are concentrated primarily in Chhattisgarh, so regional regulatory changes, infrastructure disruption, natural events, labour availability or logistics constraints can affect operations and supply chain continuity. Logistics costs, especially mining transport, are exposed to diesel price volatility as mining vehicles are predominantly fuel-dependent. Mitigants: the integrated model with captive mining and captive power, strategic inventory and logistics planning, and an EV fleet transition in mining and manufacturing.

risks.risk: Trade protectionism and global macroeconomic slowdown
risks.note: Rising trade protectionism - the US reimposition of 50% steel tariffs under Section 232 from April 2026, and the EU's CBAM - is reshaping global steel trade flows, and surplus steel diverted from protected markets may intensify competition in India's domestic market. With IMF global growth projected at 3.1% in 2026 and advanced economies at or below 1.5%, a broader slowdown could dampen infrastructure investment and steel demand. Mitigants: a predominantly domestic revenue base, projected Indian steel demand growth of +7.4% in 2026 accelerating to +9.2% in 2027, government capex of Rs.11.21 lakh crore providing a demand floor, and export optionality through CBAM-compliant gas pellets.

themes.title: Metals & mining cycle - steel, aluminium, critical minerals
themes.need: Domestic demand growth, safeguard duties and an India capacity-expansion wave lift integrated metals while critical-mineral security gains policy support. TATASTEEL targets 45-50 MT India (FY26 India EBITDA INR34,272cr at 24% margin) with a +INR6,000/t 1QFY27 realisation uplift; JINDALSTEL/SAIL/JSWSTEEL-tier on steel; HINDALCO/NALCO on aluminium; HINDZINC on zinc (Q1FY27 all-time-record EBITDA INR8,074cr +109% YoY on a record-low zinc cost-of-production USD851/t, though CEO Arun Misra hands over to ex-SAIL chief Amarendu Prakash 1-Aug-2026 and a new Gundlupet REE/Yttrium critical-minerals block won this quarter is a 2031-32-dated option, not near-term); NMDC/COALINDIA/LLOYDSME/SARDAEN on iron-ore/coal/integrated mining. Q1FY27 also quantified the export-side shock and the downstream escape from it: JINDALSAW's consolidated PAT fell 78% YoY to INR 91cr on +9% revenue because the Strait-of-Hormuz blockade suspended ALL India-origin MENA export shipments from March 2026, holding utilisation at ~60-65%; SHYAMMETL took the other route, posting INR 5,455cr revenue (+23.3%) at a multi-quarter-high 14.9% EBITDA margin with aluminium EBITDA/t +52% YoY and specialty alloys near 20.5% margin, self-funding ~INR 9,580cr of balance capex with no debt.
themes.driver: Steel price/realisation uplift into Q1; safeguard-duty support; Hormuz reopening for line-pipe exports; value-added/downstream mix; iron-ore + critical-mineral volume ramp.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: GPIL operates an integrated steel value chain that begins with captive iron ore mining and beneficiation, moves through high-grade magnetite pelletisation at Siltara, Raipur, sponge iron (DRI) and billet-making at its Steel Melting Shop, and ends in rolled long products, structural sections and hot-dip galvanised fabricated structures. Ferro alloys (silico-manganese) are manufactured through group entities at Urla Industrial Area, Raipur, while a captive renewable portfolio of solar, waste heat recovery, biomass and wind power supplies the manufacturing operations. Products are almost entirely intermediate industrial goods sold to construction and infrastructure, to the power transmission and renewable energy sector (where GPIL holds PGCIL certification), and to other steelmakers and re-rollers; exports are a negligible share of turnover.

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body: Pellets: 4.7Mn ton capacity (2Mn ton new plant commissioned Dec’25); Sponge iron: 0.65Mn ton capacity (up from 0.59Mn ton); Structural rolled: 3.75L tons FY27 target; BESS: 20GW project (Phase 1: 5-6GW FY28); Solar: 540MW total (165MW existing + 125MW by Jul’26); Mining: 4Mn ton ore mined FY26 (3.4Mn ton usable post-beneficiation)

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Mining and pellets:** Captive iron ore, High-grade magnetite iron ore pellets (approximately 65% iron content, low alumina and low phosphorus), CBAM-compliant gas-based pellets for export
- **Intermediates:** Sponge Iron (Direct Reduced Iron), Steel Billets (PGCIL-approved)
- **Finished long steel:** M.S. Rounds, H.B. (Hard Bright) Wires, Wire Rods, Structural Rolled Products - angles, channels, beams and joists, produced at RR Ispat
- **Value-added fabrication:** Galvanised Fabricated Products - hot-dip galvanised precision-engineered structures
- **Ferro alloys:** Silico-manganese
- **Power:** Captive renewable power - solar, waste heat recovery (WHRB), biomass and wind
- **Under development:** Cold Rolling Mill complex output - ZAM, galvalume, colour-coat and cold rolled coils, Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) through Godawari New Energy Private Limited

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- India is projected to be the strongest incremental steel-demand contributor at +7.4% in 2026 accelerating to +9.2% in 2027, while China's demand is expected to decline 1.5% in 2026 (World Steel Association, April 2026)
- Union Budget FY 2025-26 capital expenditure of Rs.11.21 lakh crore directed at railways, highways, urban infrastructure, housing and logistics - the highest-steel-consuming public investment categories - plus PM Gati Shakti, sustains multi-year structural steel, rebar and galvanised tower demand
- India's steel capacity expanding towards 300 MnT by 2031 against lagging domestic ore output creates an estimated 150 to 190 MnT iron ore deficit by 2031; imports have already risen from 0.05 MnT in 2023 to 10.50 MnT in 2026
- Iron ore pellet prices traded at Rs.8,500 to Rs.10,000 per tonne through FY 2025-26 with current prices around Rs.10,150 per tonne, and high-grade 65% Fe pellets earn an additional Rs.1,000 to Rs.1,500 per tonne above market rates
- Captive iron ore at Rs.2,900 per tonne versus a merchant market price of Rs.6,200 per tonne is described as a cost advantage of over Rs.3,300 per tonne that compounds as demand and prices rise
- The global EAF steelmaking market growing at approximately 12.6% CAGR over 2026-2034 structurally underpins demand for DRI-grade pellets as a substitute for scrap
- CBAM entered full operational phase from January 2026, imposing a carbon price on imports by embedded CO2 intensity - a tailwind for low-carbon, gas-produced pellets; DR-grade pellet export premium of about US$28 per tonne versus about US$13 per tonne for BF-grade
- US reimposition of 50% Section 232 steel tariffs from April 2026 diverts surplus steel toward Asia, heightening competition and the risk of oversupply and price suppression in the region
- Global steel overcapacity reached 640 MT in 2025 and is projected to rise to approximately 721 MT by 2027, with China's share of global steel exports rising from 19% in 2019 to 41% in 2025
- India's installed renewable capacity of 283.46 GW (including 150.26 GW solar) and the National Electricity Plan target of 236 GWh of storage by 2032 - a domestic BESS market of over Rs.19 lakh crores - against negligible domestic BESS manufacturing, is the import-substitution driver behind the BESS entry
- BESS container prices in India have risen from approximately Rs.70 lakh per MWh to Rs.80-85 lakh per MWh, with margins improving from the originally conceived 7 to 8% to approximately 12 to 13%
- Coated flat steel demand from solar mounting structures, EV body panels, white goods and roofing outpaces domestic production, sustaining import dependence that the CRM is designed to address; PLI 1.1 and PLI 1.2 reduce GPIL's effective cost of production and improve CRM margins
- DMISSP Policy 2025 mandates local procurement for government-funded projects, prioritising domestic coated steel producers over importers
- Market conditions remain structurally favourable for integrated producers, with players holding captive ore linkages better placed to preserve margins through scale and cost efficiency
- Ferro alloys demand is tied to steel output; the sector remains exposed to manganese and chrome ore price volatility, energy costs and the power-intensive nature of production

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Pellet margin: INR 2,000/ton conversion cost; DRI: 40% iron ore, 35% coal, 25% opex; BESS margin: 12-13% currently (conservative 7-8% assumed); mining cost: INR 3,000-3,200/ton; freight saving: INR 150/ton post-beneficiation at mine

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Net cash position INR 837cr; capex prioritized for BESS, steel plant, solar; no dividend policy mentioned; focus on debt-free growth and vertical integration

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: FY 2025-26 was framed as the year GPIL secured the approvals and commissioned the assets that unlock its next growth phase, with the Board approving four major strategic initiatives that together form a growth roadmap towards a revenue target of approximately Rs.30,000 crores by 2031. The 2 MnT iron ore pellet plant was commissioned in December 2025, lifting total pellet capacity 74% from 2.7 MnT to 4.7 MnT; it is described as the first plant in India to deploy natural gas-based Grate-Kiln pelletisation, replacing coal gas and cutting CO2 by roughly 2 lakh tonnes a year. Q4 FY 2025-26 was its first full quarter, at 78% utilisation, guided to 85% in FY27. On the mining side, Consent to Operate for the Ari Dongri iron ore mines at an enhanced 6 MnT was received from CECB in February 2026 (up from 2.35 MnT), described as the single most important de-risking event of the year and taking total captive ore capacity to 6.7 MnT including Boria Tibu 0.7 MnT; phased ramp-up begins in FY27 with full-scale operations targeted from FY28. A beneficiation plant at the mine site received Environment Clearance and Consent to Set Up on 31 January 2026 for expansion from 2.35 MnT to 6 MnT, with commissioning targeted for Q3 FY 2026-27. Other Consents to Operate received in the year enhanced sponge iron capacity from 0.594 MnT to 0.65 MnT, HB Wire from 0.1 MnT to 0.115 MnT, and added 7 MW of waste heat recovery power to take total WHRP capacity to 49 MW. Three build-out projects follow. The 0.7 MnT CRM Complex at Sarora (Tilda, Raipur) for cold rolled, GL/ZAM, Alu Silicon/GI and colour-coated steel carries a capex of Rs.900 crore funded by Rs.550 crore of sanctioned bank debt plus internal accruals, on 452 acres already acquired and shared with the Integrated Steel Plant, and is registered under PLI 1.1 and PLI 1.2; equipment orders have been placed for the Pickling Line, two CGL lines, the Colour Coating Line and the Acid Regeneration Plant. The 1 MnT Integrated Steel Plant for structural steel and wire rods via the blast furnace route is envisaged at Rs.7,000 crores on a 1:1 debt-equity basis, with environment approval granted and Consent to Establish awaited. A 20 GWh BESS manufacturing plant is being executed through 100% subsidiary Godawari New Energy Private Limited on 112 acres in the AURIC Industrial Area, Maharashtra, with Maharashtra government incentives approved and a Tier-1 supply chain secured (EVE Power LFP cells, ROCHE Energy BOS, FIMER India PCS); the Directors' Report separately describes a 40 GWh BESS project in two phases at a total cost of Rs.1625 crores including working capital margin money, plus a 45 MWh BESS at the Mahurmkala solar plant for about Rs.40 crores. Captive solar is being tripled from 165 MW to 540 MW to power the mines, the additional pellet capacity, the CRM and the ISP: 25 MW commissioned, 100 MW under construction, and 250 MW with land in possession aligned to ISP and CRM commissioning. CAUTION - the bundle carries internally inconsistent dates and quanta for the same projects: the CRM is variously given commissioning of August 2027 (Corporate Overview initiative panel), March 2027 (Chairman deep-dive and project table) and construction start of August 2026 versus July 2026; the ISP construction start is given as November 2026 in one place and October 2026 in another with commissioning targeted FY 2029-30; the 100 MW solar is given commissioning of July 2026 in the Corporate Overview and Q2FY27 in the Directors' Report; the 25 MW solar is dated May 2026 in the Directors' Report and 19 May 2026 in the Corporate Overview; and BESS capex appears as Rs.1,400 crores (Corporate Overview / Chairman) and Rs.1625 crores for the full 40 GWh in the Directors' Report. Existing captive solar is stated as 165 MW in the Corporate Overview but the MD&A describes a renewable portfolio of 190 MW of solar.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Confident, forward-looking, and execution-focused; transparent on CAPEX revisions; emphasizes decarbonization, export readiness, and vertical integration; acknowledges Q1 price softening but remains bullish on long-term demand

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Backward integration into captive iron ore: captive ore at Rs.2,900 per tonne versus a merchant market price of Rs.6,200 per tonne, described as a cost advantage of over Rs.3,300 per tonne
- Long-life captive resource base - estimated reserve of 165 million tonnes and mine life exceeding 35 years, with mining capacity enhanced to 6.7 million tonnes in 2026
- Product quality premium: low-alumina, low-phosphorus 65% Fe pellets command a realisation premium of Rs.1,000 to Rs.1,500 per tonne over market rates
- India's first natural gas-based Grate-Kiln pellet plant (2 MnT), producing inherently CBAM-compliant, export-ready pellets and cutting CO2 by roughly 2 lakh tonnes per annum versus coal-based processes
- PGCIL approval for billets and galvanised structures - GPIL is one of a small number of Indian steel producers holding it for transmission projects
- Captive renewable power portfolio of 190 MW solar, 28.5 MW biomass, 49 MW waste heat recovery and 1.5 MW wind, lowering per-unit energy cost and carbon intensity in an energy-intensive industry
- Healthy net cash position backing a strategically structured capex plan
- CRM complex registered under both PLI 1.1 and PLI 1.2, described as a significant advantage versus non-PLI-registered competitors
- Secured Tier-1 BESS supply chain - EVE Power (LFP cells), ROCHE Energy (BOS), FIMER India and Hopewind (PCS) - plus comprehensive Maharashtra government incentives
- Structural products carry a healthy order book of six months serving EPC contractors in the power and infrastructure sectors
- High utilisation and internal synergies - pellet operations ran at 95% capacity utilisation, and CRM output is designed to supply steel containers to the Company's own BESS facility

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Iron ore price volatility; BESS component cost inflation (lithium); delays in steel plant commissioning; export market access; regulatory delays in environmental clearances; global steel demand slowdown

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: BESS margins are higher than initially modeled (12-13% vs 7-8%) due to Indian grid instability demand; EV fleet adoption cut diesel costs by 75% and emissions by 88%; pellet premium pricing will emerge post-monsoon (Q3) as high-grade output rises; INR 100cr CAPEX saved by switching from coal gasification to natural gas for pellets

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Vision 2030] Backed by a strong balance sheet and captive mining assets, the deck targets approximately 4x revenue (Rs 5,381 Cr in FY26 to Rs 24,000 Cr in 2030E), ~3x EBITDA (Rs 1,253 Cr to Rs 3,500 Cr) and ~3x PAT (Rs 802 Cr to Rs 2,500 Cr).
- [Macro headwind] Sequential profitability was hit by elevated coal prices and increased market sourcing of iron ore following the West Asia crisis - a named external shock, not an operating deterioration.
- [State incentives] The Maharashtra Government approved multiple incentives for the BESS project including electricity duty and stamp duty exemptions, power tariff subsidy, interest and capital subsidies, SGST-linked incentives and ESI/EPF reimbursements.
- [Shareholding] Promoter and Promoter Group hold 63.18% as on 30-Jun-26, with FPI at 6.00%, domestic institutions 3.10% and non-institution 27.72% of 67,30,97,430 total shares.
- [Workforce] Attrition of 4.6%, average employee age 42 years and average tenure 10 years; term insurance for 100% of employees, group medical cover for 91%; Great Place to Work certified.
